title: A preliminary blowup produces a fibrewise nonempty free locus
statement: Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme, $f:X\to S$ an affine, flat morphism of finite presentation, and $\mathcal F$ a finite-type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. Assume every fibre of $f$ is geometrically integral, meaning integral after every field extension. Let $U\subset S$ be a quasi-compact open such that $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$ is of finite presentation and $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ at the generic point of each fibre over $U$. Then there is a $U$-admissible blowup $b:S^b\to S$ and an open $V\subset X\times_SS^b$ such that $V\to S^b$ is surjective and the module strict transform $\mathcal F^b|_V$ is finite locally free, meaning locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_V^{\oplus r}$ for a finite integer $r$ which may vary between open subsets. The morphism notions, admissibility and strict transform are as in [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [def-nagata-admissible-blowup], [def-trf-module-strict-transform].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-generic-rank-admissible-invariance] to the given family and module. We obtain finitely many quasi-compact clopen generic-rank strata $U_i$ of $U$, and freeness of the stalks at all fibre generic points over each $U_i$ with its fixed rank $r_i$.

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, proof paragraph defining the locally constant generic rank.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-rank-partition-cartier-charts] to this partition. It gives a $U$-admissible blowup $b:S_1\to S$ and finitely many affine opens $W_j=\operatorname{Spec}R_j$ covering $S_1$, with $U_1\cap W_j=D(h_j)$ for a nonzerodivisor $h_j$ and with $W_j$ meeting only one rank stratum $U_{i(j)}$. Here $U_1=b^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact, since admissibility identifies it with $U$. By [lem-trf-generic-rank-admissible-invariance], the family $X_1=X\times_SS_1$ and strict transform $\mathcal F_1$ retain all the affine, flat, finite presentation, geometric integrality and finite-type hypotheses; over $U_1$ the original finitely presented module and generic free stalks are unchanged.

source.place: Tags 0811 (lemma-flatten-module-pre, rank separation) and 080Y (remark-successive-blowups, Cartier-boundary reduction).

proof.text: On each $W_j$, the hypotheses of [lem-trf-affine-free-blowup-realization] hold for $(R_j,h_j,X_1|_{W_j},\mathcal F_1|_{X_1|_{W_j}},r_{i(j)})$. Indeed finite presentation on $D(h_j)$ and the constant free rank at its fibre generic points were supplied in the preceding steps. Thus we obtain a $(U_1\cap W_j)$-admissible blowup $T_j\to W_j$ and a fibrewise surjective open $V_j$ on which the corresponding strict transform is finite locally free of rank $r_{i(j)}$.

source.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre, final proof paragraph, applying Tag 0810 (lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space).

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-admissible-local-free-gluing] for the finite affine cover $(W_j)$ of the qcqs base $S_1$, its quasi-compact open $U_1$, the flat family $X_1\to S_1$, the finite-type quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F_1$, and the witnesses $(T_j,V_j)$. It gives a $U_1$-admissible blowup $c:T\to S_1$ with comparison maps $c_j:T\times_{S_1}W_j\to T_j$. Define $V$ as the union of the inverse images of $V_j$ under the induced maps on the base-changed family. The cited statement identifies the successive strict transform on each inverse image with the pullback of the finite locally free module on $V_j$, and states that this union is surjective over $T$. Hence that transform is finite locally free on $V$, viewed in $X\times_ST$ through the canonical fibre-product identification.

source.place: Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, final paragraph: locality on the base and domination of local blowups.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus] (1), the composite $b\circ c$ is the blowup of a finite-type ideal with zero set $Z\cup b(Z_1)$, where $Z,Z_1$ are the two centres. Both terms miss $U$, since $Z$ misses $U$ and $Z_1$ misses $b^{-1}(U)$; thus this blowup is $U$-admissible. The same clause identifies its module strict transform with the successive transform. Take $S^b=T$ and the same $V$. If the Cartier reduction gives an empty base, the empty open is surjective onto it.

source.place: Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups, paragraph on composition of finite-type blowups and their module strict transforms.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0811, lemma-flatten-module-pre; Tag 080Y, remark-successive-blowups. The boundary is principalized before separating ranks, allowing reuse of the existing separation-of-closures theorem.
